New installations now use a Btrfs root filesystem, which grows to the selected VM disk size on boot. The legacy `rootfs.ext4.zst` download name is retained for launcher and backup compatibility; the filesystem inside is Btrfs.

The guest now includes clipboard support. In the default text console:

```sh
printf 'hello' | try-arch-clipboard copy
try-arch-clipboard paste
```

Copy reads UTF-8 text from stdin; paste prints Windows clipboard text to stdout. Text is limited to 8 MiB. The console does not have desktop selection or Ctrl+V paste. Compatible Wayland desktops can share text, images and files through the included clipboard service. The service starts with `graphical-session.target`; other compatible sessions can start it with `systemctl --user start try-arch-clipboard`.

Download **TryArch.exe** for new installations. Updating the launcher preserves existing Linux disks and does not convert ext4 to Btrfs or install new guest software. Back up your Linux files before using Start fresh; it replaces the existing guest disk.

The release pipeline checks the guest contract, boots the rebuilt guest, verifies Btrfs and disk growth, and runs launcher tests before uploading assets. Automatic Wayland clipboard sharing still depends on the installed desktop's clipboard protocol support.

Windows 10/11 on Intel/AMD x86_64 with Windows Hypervisor Platform is required. The launcher is unsigned and automatic updates remain disabled. Kernel package upgrades still require matching external kernel/initramfs assets.
